races.title: State House, District 108
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: John A. Torbett
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 108 (Gaston County) since 2010. Gaston County Commissioner 2002–2010. Business executive: long career in the corrugated converting industry, then vice president roles at defense-technology firms, including Defense Technologies, Inc.
cands.gaps: We could not find Torbett's birthplace, where he was raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. His campaign biography lists East Ridge High School (class of 1974) and Middle Tennessee State University (1975–77) without saying where he grew up. We found no documented stance by him on data centers or on development, and no endorsements for the 2026 race. We found no news reporting of controversies. We found no bill sponsorship or official-record deeds tied to the issues voters care about, so his issue positions here come only from his own campaign site. His site's issues page was cut off partway through the jobs and economy section, so anything after that point was not read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: 16 years in the NC House (since 2010), including Appropriations vice chair, after two terms as Gaston County Commissioner (2002–2010). Earlier career in corrugated converting from 1978, rising through plant manager to CEO, then business-development and operations roles at defense-technology firms.
qual.why: Long prior legislative service with budget-writing roles and local elected office, plus management and executive experience in business, places him in the high band for a job of writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: Long prior legislative service with budget-writing roles and local elected office, plus management and executive experience in business, places him in the high band for a job of writing law and the state budget.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says on his campaign site that parents, not a system, should have the ultimate choice on where their children attend school, and that he has supported efforts to increase teacher pay and education funding.

workers-first.evidence: Says on his campaign site that people entering the country illegally should be charged and sentenced and not allowed to stay or re-enter for a significant period, and that border security should be strengthened. He also says law-abiding immigrants should have a path through current law.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Sydnie Hutchinson
cands.bio: Paralegal since 2014 in personal injury, wrongful death, family law and workers' compensation. Earlier worked as a restaurant server, bartender and manager. Gaston County Democratic Party 3rd vice chair. Democratic nominee for NC House District 108 in 2024 and 2026. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Jamie Fowler, Ranlo Town Commissioner, was listed as an endorser in her 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

cands.gaps: We could not find when she moved back to North Carolina or where she was raised. She says she graduated from Highland High School in Gilbert, Arizona in 2010 and lived in South Carolina and Indiana before returning, but gives no dates for the return. She has held no elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no statements from her on data centers, development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, policing, gun laws, immigration or H-1B, or school vouchers and charters. Her statements on teacher pay and public school funding are about public schools only. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so her stated positions come from her 2024 survey and her campaign website. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Paralegal since 2014 in personal injury, wrongful death, family law and workers' compensation; earlier worked in restaurant service and management; held party posts in Gaston County (3rd vice chair, Young Democrats vice president); has not held elected office.
qual.why: Her law-office work gives some exposure to how legislation affects people, and she has management experience. She has no legislative service or elected office and is not a lawyer, so she scores in the middle range.
qual.label: Her law-office work gives some exposure to how legislation affects people, and she has management experience. She has no legislative service or elected office and is not a lawyer, so she scores in the middle range.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Said on her campaign site that corporate landlords with large capital should be stopped from buying up single-family homes and neighborhoods, and that there must be a cap on this, especially in Gaston County.

pro-life.evidence: Said on her campaign site that she will fight restrictions on women's healthcare and prevent government overreach on women's reproductive healthcare.
